facts.text: Antioch was renamed after the biblical city in 1851 when the town’s minister suggested the name to honor early Christian settlers.
Coal discoveries south of Antioch in 1859 sparked the founding of nearby towns like Black Diamond, boosting regional mining activity.
In the late 1800s, Antioch’s Chinese residents faced forced segregation, even being barred from walking the streets after sundown.
The City of Antioch launched Rivertown Free Wi‑Fi on April 21, 2026, offering free wireless access across historic Rivertown blocks.
Gateway Generating Station, a 530‑MW natural‑gas plant, began delivering power to Antioch residents in January 2009.
A Bay Area Rapid Transit station opened in Antioch in May 2018, connecting the city directly to the greater San Francisco Bay Area.
